..
As of 245 PM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1....Rain tapers off this afternoon into this evening. 
Much cooler tonight through early next week. Patchy frost is 
possible late Sunday night in sheltered, rural Piedmont locations.

Early this afternoon, a seasonally strong cold front pushed offshore 
of the mid-Atlantic coast. Strong cold air advection in the wake of 
this front has allowed much cooler air to filter into the region on 
gusty N winds. Widespread stratiform rain overrunning the boundary 
has begun clearing across western zones. Expect the remainder of the 
area to dry out over the next few hours, though clearing will take 
longer across Southside Hampton Roads into NE NC, where light rain 
may linger into early evening. Decreasing clouds west of I-95 will 
allow for late-day sun and modest warming before sunset, though 
temperatures will generally hold in the mid to upper 50s.

The mid/upper-level trough pushes toward the coast this evening, 
then closes off offshore tonight as strong 1030+ mb surface high 
pressure builds in from the northwest. Continued cool/dry air 
advection will maintain inland clearing, with drying conditions 
reaching the coast. Overnight lows will drop into the 40s to 
near 50 along the immediate coast, with upper 30s to lower 40s 
inland. A well-mixed boundary layer (winds lingering 5-10 mph) 
should prevent temperatures from completely bottoming out, 
therefore minimizing the potential for patchy frost, even across
the piedmont. A partly to mostly sunny and breezy Fall day is 
ahead for tomorrow. Despite plenty of sunshine, highs only in 
the upper 50s to lower 60s are forecast. As high pressure 
settles just NNW of the area Sunday night, a better chance for 
patchy frost arises across the far NW Piedmont, followed by 
highs in the 60s on Monday.

 
KEY MESSAGE 2...Breezy N to NE winds are expected through early
next week, especially along the immediate coast where gusty 
conditions will persist into midweek. A Wind Advisory remains in
effect for Virginia Beach and Currituck County, NC into Sunday 
morning.

Low pressure continues to develop along the offshore front near
Cape Hatteras this afternoon. The tightening pressure gradient 
between this developing low and the 1030+ mb high to our 
northwest will maintain northerly winds of 15 to 20 mph inland, 
with gusts of 20 to 30 mph. Along the coast, NE winds of 25 to 
30 mph with gusts of 40 to 50 mph will continue into Sunday, 
highest from Virginia Beach south to the NC Northern Outer 
Banks.

As the cold front shifts farther offshore, confidence continues
to increase that the coastal low/nor'easter will deepen further
through the first half of next week. The low is forecast to 
meander offshore of the Carolina/lower mid-Atlantic coast 
through at least midweek, resulting in persistent breezy 
conditions inland and prolonged windy conditions along the 
immediate coast. N-NE gusts will average 20 to 30 mph inland and
30 to 45 mph along the coast, highest over the Virginia Capes 
south to the NC Northern Outer Banks.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Forecast uncertainty remains early next week 
regarding the track and intensity of the nor'easter offshore. 
Regardless of model spread, a long-duration coastal flood event 
is expected. Coastal Flood Advisories continue for this 
afternoon's high tide cycle, with Coastal Flood Watches in 
effect for Monday's high tides across the lower Chesapeake Bay, 
lower James River, and the Atlantic coast of the Eastern Shore.

Model guidance exhibits spread regarding cyclone intensity and 
placement, particularly beyond Tuesday. With the cutoff low 
detached from the primary jet stream and lacking an upstream 
kicker trough, probabilistic ensembles favor a system meandering
offshore through midweek. Gale-force N-NE winds will drive 
building tidal anomalies over the next few days, initially 
generating minor flooding in the lower Bay and lower James River
with the upcoming high tide.

Prolonged onshore flow will drive anomalies to 1 to 3 feet 
above normal astronomical tide. Fortunately, the region is 
currently in an astronomical neap tide cycle, which will help to
mitigate peak water levels. Even so, widespread minor to 
moderate coastal flooding is expected during high tides through 
early next week, peaking on Monday. If the low strengthens 
further or edges closer to the coast, localized major flooding 
cannot be ruled out, though consensus guidance continues to 
trend "lower" toward high-end minor to moderate thresholds. 
Coastal Flood Watches have been expanded to include the Atlantic
side of the Eastern Shore, including Ocean City.
